transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Sara Thompson (Bluefin Head of ML), Diego Alvarez (Bluefin Infra), Priya Menon (Bluefin SecOps), Tom Reynolds (Bluefin PM)

Summary:
Quick POC weekly sync focused on onboarding progress, access setup, and environment readiness. Covered outstanding infra gating items (SSO, KMS, VPC peering), review of initial benchmark numbers (preliminary p95 ~220ms for small batch, discussion about KV cache warmup), and next steps to run a larger 1k request benchmark. Agreed to share security docs and schedule a KMS deep-dive.

Topics:
- Access & creds (SSO/SAML, bastion, service accounts)
- Network (VPC peering, egress rules, certs)
- Security (KMS, audit logs, SOC2 scope)
- Benchmarks (throughput, p50/p95/p99, cold vs warm KV cache)
- Rollout plan (canary, fallback to hosted)

Action items (high level): see metadata.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jenna Park: All right, hello everyone, thanks for doing the Friday sync, quick check-in on the pilot orbit. um Marcus and I are here from Redwood. How's everybody doing over there?
[00:08] Sara Thompson: Good, thanks. We had a couple folks in meetings, but we should be able to run through this. Excited to see the benchmark details.
[00:12] Marcus Li: Great. I'll lead the perf bits. Just to set expectation, today's goal is to confirm access, clarify KMS plan, and agree on a timeline for the 1k-run.
[00:20] Diego Alvarez: On our side we finished the initial peering setup but there was a minor routing issue — the bastion couldn't reach the probe container without an explicit egress rule. We pushed a fix at 10:00.
[00:30] Jenna Park: Okay perfect. Diego, can you confirm the CIDR ranges and the firewall rules so Marcus can run the external probe?
[00:36] Diego Alvarez: Yep I'll drop the CIDR and the SSH key in the shared doc after the call.
[00:40] Tom Reynolds: Quick question — are you expecting the KV cache to be warm for the bench? Our traffic pattern will be very bursty during our test.
[00:48] Marcus Li: Good question. For the 1k synthetic run we should do two passes: cold start to see base modelload + kv-grab, and then warm pass to measure steady-state p95. Right now our small test showed p95 around 220ms on warm runs, cold was closer to 380ms because of kv cache miss and model init jitter.
[01:05] Sara Thompson: 220ms p95 is acceptable for our interactive use cases. But what's the CPU/GPU configuration for that run?
[01:12] Marcus Li: That was on one A100 equivalent GPU in Redwood Dedicated infra, 8k context but model trimmed to 2k for test. Batch size 4, continuous batching enabled. We didn't push quantization profiles yet — that's next.
[01:24] Priya Menon: On the security side, we need clarity on where keys are stored. Are you supporting KMS via customer-managed keys? We have an internal policy that requires HSM-backed keys.
[01:34] Jenna Park: We support integration with customer KMS, and for the private offering we can do HSM/KMS policies. I'll share the KMS integration notes and the HSM options — also include an example key policy.
[01:44] Priya Menon: Also need to see audit log samples, retention windows, and any downsampling that Redwood does for analytics. We can't have raw payloads stored unencrypted.
[01:53] Jenna Park: Totally. We'll share the SOC2 artifacts and a sample audit log export. The logs redact sensitive fields by default but we can show exact retention tiers.
[01:59] Speaker 5: (mumbled) do we have any SLA numbers around rollout and error sway during canary?
[02:05] Marcus Li: For the Dedicated plan we target p99 latency SLOs and a 99.9% uptime SLA. For canary rollouts we recommend a weighted traffic approach with automatic fallback to the previous model variant on error rate > threshold.
[02:18] Tom Reynolds: If we end up needing Private deployment, what's the lift? Ballpark time and blockers?
[02:23] Jenna Park: Private deployment is more involved — network setup, KMS hookups, and the install window. Typical lead time is 4–8 weeks depending on KMS/HSM approvals and audit access. But we can do a VPC-hosted private control plane in 2–3 weeks if networking is straightforward.
[02:37] Diego Alvarez: That aligns with our internal timeline. We have change freeze starting 4/20, so if we want Private in April it'd be tight.
[02:44] Marcus Li: For the immediate pilot let's keep Hosted/Dedicated with VPC peering and customer KMS — that gives you double isolation with lower setup than full private.
[02:54] Sara Thompson: Sounds good. Regarding the benchmark spreadsheet you mentioned, can you explain the columns and what to look for?
[02:59] Marcus Li: Sure. The sheet will include: test_id, timestamp, request_size, batch_size, p50/p95/p99, throughput rps, GPU util, KV hit-rate, and errors per minute. We'll highlight warm vs cold passes and annotate any retries.
[03:14] Tom Reynolds: Also can you include cost estimates per 10k requests in that sheet? We need to compare to our current service.
[03:20] Jenna Park: We will. We'll add a cost-per-1k token and an estimated monthly run-rate based on your expected QPS.
[03:25] Priya Menon: On SSO, our IdP team needs SAML metadata. Diego, can you coordinate that with Jenna after the call?
[03:31] Diego Alvarez: Yep will do. I'll put the metadata and a test account in the shared drive.
[03:34] Jenna Park: Great. For the KMS deep-dive, Marcus can join. We'll walk through envelope encryption, key rotation, and sample policies.
[03:42] Marcus Li: One note on KV cache — you'll want to pre-warm the cache with a representative prompt set. We can provide our cache-warming script that posts a seed corpus; it avoids the long tail cold misses on first-run.
[03:52] Sara Thompson: That would be helpful. For our prompt set there are about 600 unique prefixes, so we should probably do two rounds.
[04:00] Marcus Li: Two rounds should give you >95% warm-hit rate on the second pass. We'll include the script in the repo.
[04:07] Tom Reynolds: Any blockers around cert installation? We tried to upload a wildcard cert and it failed with an error about chain.
[04:13] Jenna Park: We'll check the cert chain. Usually that's due to missing intermediate certs; send the PEM bundle and we'll validate.
[04:18] Diego Alvarez: I'll attach the bundle.
[04:21] Speaker 5: (overlap) do we have a rough timeline for the 1k benchmark?
[04:25] Marcus Li: We can run it Friday morning. I need the SSO test account for one auth path and the peering confirmed for probes. If Diego shares CIDR and the bastion key today, we can run Friday US morning.
[04:36] Sara Thompson: Friday works. Let's plan for midday UTC so we can observe from Europe too.
[04:40] Jenna Park: Noted. After the run we'll upload the raw CSV and a highlighted summary.
[04:45] Priya Menon: A few security clarifications: do you persist request logs with PII? We need explicit guarantees.
[04:52] Marcus Li: By default we do not persist unredacted PII; customers can opt-in for longer retention, but for your account we'll enforce redaction and short retention unless you request otherwise. We'll document this in the security packet.
[05:05] Sara Thompson: Good. Also would like to see a sample incident response timeline if there is a data incident.
[05:10] Jenna Park: We'll include an incident response playbook summary and a named contact list.
[05:14] Tom Reynolds: On the product side, can we validate the function calling behavior for structured outputs? We rely on toolcalls for entity extraction.
[05:22] Marcus Li: Yes, part of the functional bench we'll run a subset of prompt tests with function calls and measure error rates and schema mismatches. Expect a small extra latency per call since there's serialization overhead.
[05:33] Sara Thompson: How do you handle model rollbacks if a new model shows regressions?
[05:37] Marcus Li: We do canary rollouts with monitored metrics (quality regressions from your eval set + error spikes). If regressions exceed thresholds we automatically shift traffic back and send alerts.
[05:46] Diego Alvarez: For telemetry, what hooks do we need to add to our infra to collect traces?
[05:50] Marcus Li: We support OpenTelemetry and HTTP headers for trace context. We'll share the tracing spec — it's a simple agent and an endpoint to forward to.
[05:58] Speaker 5: (inaudible) so after Friday's run what's the next major milestone?
[06:02] Jenna Park: If the 1k benchmarks look good, we move to a 7-day pilot with a production-like workload and start canary rollouts for the first feature. That would be early May given current timelines.
[06:12] Sara Thompson: Sounds reasonable. 
[06:14] Tom Reynolds: Anything else on access?
[06:16] Diego Alvarez: No, I'll post the peering details and the bastion key.
[06:19] Jenna Park: I'll send the security packet and schedule the KMS deep-dive. Marcus will run the 1k-run and post results.
[06:24] Sara Thompson: Thanks all.
[06:26] Jenna Park: Great, thanks team — we'll follow up in the shared doc and set up the KMS call.

(Conversation ends at ~52:00)
